message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **federal statutory holidays that create “long weekends” in Canada during 2023**.  
(If a holiday falls on a weekend, the *observed* day is usually the following Monday; that observed day is what makes the long weekend.)

| Holiday | 2023 Date | Observed (if weekend) | Long‑Weekend Period (Sat–Sun–Mon) | Notes |
|---------|-----------|-----------------------|-----------------------------------|-------|
| **Family Day** (Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Ontario, New Brunswick, Manitoba, Prince Edward Island) | Feb 20 (Mon) | — | **Feb 18–20** | Creates a 3‑day weekend. |
| **Good Friday** (all provinces) | Apr 7 (Fri) | — | **Apr 7–9** | Friday + weekend. |
| **Victoria Day** (all provinces) | May 22 (Mon) | — | **May 20–22** | Monday + weekend. |
| **Canada Day** (all provinces) | Jul 1 (Sat) | Jul 3 (Mon) | **Jul 1–3** | Holiday on Saturday → observed Monday. |
| **Labour Day** (all provinces) | Sep 4 (Mon) | — | **Sep 2–4** | Monday + weekend. |
| **Thanksgiving** (all provinces) | Oct 9 (Mon) | — | **Oct 7–9** | Monday + weekend. |
| **Remembrance Day** (all provinces) | Nov 11 (Thu) | — | **Nov 11–13** | Thursday + weekend (Thu‑Fri‑Sat). |
| **Christmas Day** (all provinces) | Dec 25 (Mon) | — | **Dec 23–25** | Monday + weekend. |
| **Boxing Day** (all provinces) | Dec 26 (Tue) | — | **Dec 24–26** | Tuesday + weekend (Sun‑Mon‑Tue). |

> **Quick recap:**  
> • If a holiday falls on **Monday**, the long weekend is the preceding Saturday–Sunday–Monday.  
> • If it falls on **Friday**, the long weekend is Friday–Saturday–Sunday.  
> • If it falls on **Saturday** or **Sunday**, the holiday is observed on the following Monday, giving a long weekend that includes the weekend and the observed Monday.  
> • If it falls on **Thursday** (e.g., Remembrance Day), the long weekend extends to the following Saturday (Thu‑Fri‑Sat).  

These are the federal holidays that will give you a 3‑day break in 2023. If you’re interested in provincial holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. George’s Day in New Brunswick, etc.), let me know and I can add those too.
